summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was admitted for evaluation of chest pain, abdominal distention, and bilateral lower extremity edema. Initial assessment ruled out cardiac ischemia with normal cardiac enzymes and a negative stress test. Chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal in origin. Abdominal imaging showed no ascites or complete bowel obstruction, with mild distention likely due to partial bowel slowing. He was volume overloaded, prompting an additional dose of Lasix, while maintaining his baseline diuretic regimen. His condition improved, and he was discharged home on unchanged medications with plans for outpatient follow-up in primary care and hepatology.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission
Need for prophylactic vaccination and inoculation against influenza
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
